units.function: A 3398-line worker-to-host implementation exposing configuration, filesystem, state, SQL, entities, events, HTTP, Secrets, telemetry, organization/task data, approvals, Agents, Goals, access administration, authorization policy and Agent sessions.
units.dependencyDirection: Directly composes most server domain services, database tables, storage, networking, telemetry, worker/event infrastructure and plugin SDK types; capability enforcement lives outside this object in a separate dispatcher.
units.keyDataModels: Company/Agent/Project/Issue/Goal/Approval, human/agent actor IDs, plugin/company state, SQL, Secret refs, invite/grant/policy, attachment bytes, Agent session/live events and operational telemetry.
units.lifecycle: Builds one instance-wide plugin facade, accepts company/resource/actor parameters from worker calls, performs reads and high-impact mutations, records plugin activity, forwards events, buffers logs and disposes subscriptions best-effort.
units.testAssessment: The five focused access/authorization cases all skipped locally. Other separate tests cover spans and scoped routing, but this unit lacks a complete operation-by-operation capability/tenant/actor/data matrix and adversarial SSRF, resource-limit, impersonation, session-isolation and failure-recovery proof.
units.designRationale: Give plugin authors a rich typed SDK while reusing core services, preserving company equality checks and adding targeted safety helpers such as DNS pinning, redaction and provider-span clamping.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs narrow ports whose authority is host-minted per invocation from authenticated principal, approved Connector grant, Responsibility contract and DataAuthorization, with every mutation/effect producing durable evidence.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT the monolithic facade and caller-supplied authority model. Selectively reference provider-span clamping, DNS pinning, non-oracle tenant responses and active-membership checks as defense-in-depth; split Company OS interfaces by capability and require a non-forgeable InvocationAuthority object that services cannot bypass.
units.responsibilityConflict: A plugin can name an eligible human and have approvals/comments/interactions attributed to them without proof of intent; plugins are instance-wide with no company grant; high-risk access/policy/Agent actions lack exact human approval; entity/SQL/state/session paths have cross-tenant or wildcard hazards and data egress is not purpose-bound.
evidence: 9ace548f feat(observability): rename sandbox provider spans and add run-time wrapper spans (#10999)

units.function: Embedded-database tests for plugin-driven grant targeting, invite redaction, authorization audit search, protected-Agent policy decisions and policy sanitization/activity attribution.
units.dependencyDirection: Calls buildHostServices directly with plugin identity and database/event stubs, bypassing worker dispatcher capability and invocation-scope layers.
units.keyDataModels: Company membership, Agent, invite token/defaults, permission grants, authorization policy/decision and activity log.
units.lifecycle: Seeds companies/principals, invokes administrative HostServices methods, verifies cross-company rejection/redaction/policy behavior and inspects persistence/activity.
units.testAssessment: All five cases skipped due unavailable embedded PostgreSQL. Assertions are useful lower-layer regressions but cannot prove an installed plugin was granted the operation, the actor was authenticated, or a human approved the exact change.
units.designRationale: Harden new plugin administration surfaces against obvious tenant mismatch, secret leakage and policy bypass.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs end-to-end responsibility tests from authenticated human intent or governed Agent action through a non-forgeable invocation grant and exact durable evidence.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the two-company fixtures, secret-redaction negatives, policy-deny invariants and plugin-source audit assertions; add capability denial, forged human/board actor, exact approval digest, grant expiry, concurrency, legal retention and failure/outbox cases.
units.responsibilityConflict: The test itself supplies human actor IDs to plugin methods and treats active membership as sufficient attribution; createInvite, grants and policy writes require no accountable approval or package/grant binding.
